subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Skimming, True/False/Not Given and vocabulary development / Pronouns as cohesive devices, the Wright brothers and timed reading
outcomes: Skim a text and choose the best title
Answer True / False / Not Given and find what pronouns refer to
Read against the clock for speed and accuracy

tf.s: Skimming means reading quickly to get the general idea.
tf.why: Yes, skimming gives you the main idea.

tf.s: 'Not Given' means the text does not give that information.
tf.why: Correct, the text does not say.

tf.s: Title d covers only one section of the text.
tf.why: That is why it is not the best title.

tf.s: Scanning is the same as skimming.
tf.why: Skimming is for the main idea; scanning is for details.

tf.s: Title a was chosen because it is very general.
tf.why: Titles a and b were rejected because they are too general.

tf.s: A good title should match the whole text.
tf.why: Yes, it should cover the main idea of all sections.

tf.s: 'It' can refer back to a noun in an earlier sentence.
tf.why: Yes, pronouns link back to nouns.

tf.s: Timed reading measures your reading speed and accuracy.
tf.why: Right, you record your speed and your score.

tf.s: In a True/False/Not Given task, you correct the statements that are true.

boxes.why: Title c covers the whole text.

o: It refers to only one section
boxes.why: A title must cover the whole text.

boxes.q: In the text, what does 'they' refer to?
In the text, what does 'them' refer to?

boxes.why: Statement d was false because of this detail.

boxes.q: Who is the timed reading about?
boxes.why: The Wright brothers were flying pioneers.

boxes.q: What job do pronouns do in a text?
What do you work out after timed reading?
o: Words per minute and your score

hunt.q: Reading fast for the main idea
Fuel tested by airlines in the text
Among the first to do something new
The best title for the text

mcq.q: What do pronouns do in a text?
o: They link phrases and sentences so the text reads smoothly

mcq.q: What should you note carefully in True/False/Not Given tasks?
o: Adverbs and qualifying words like 'partly' and 'entirely'
mcq.why: Small words can change the meaning.

o: A person who is among the first to do something new
mcq.why: The Wright brothers were flying pioneers.

mcq.q: What was the Virgin Atlantic flight?
o: The world's first commercial biofuel flight
mcq.why: It was partly powered by biofuel.

mcq.q: The text says the plane was partly powered by biofuel. Statement: 'The plane used only biofuel.' What is the answer?
The text says nothing about the pilot's age. Statement: 'The pilot was 40 years old.' What is the answer?
mcq.why: If the text does not say it, choose Not Given.

mcq.q: Which word is the verb of 'invention'?
mcq.why: Invent is the verb; inventor is the person.

mcq.q: Why were titles a and b rejected?
o: They are the same as title c
mcq.why: A good title is specific to the text.

mcq.q: Why do we answer the questions after finishing a timed reading?
o: So the questions do not distract us from reading
mcq.why: You measure pure reading speed first.

mcq.q: Why is a pronoun often better than repeating 'biofuel' again and again?
o: It makes the text smoother and less repetitive
